name: PA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: No polling or expert ratings available
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~97%
model.rationale: The district's R+19 lean, Meuser's incumbency, and his clear fundraising advantage over Rachel Wallace all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and prediction markets price a Republican win around 97%. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, only a modest adjustment from the fundamentals is warranted.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Meuser underperforming the district's lean, or a surge of Democratic outside spending, would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Dan Meuser seeks another term in a northeastern Pennsylvania district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan lean of about 19 points toward the GOP. He was renominated without difficulty and has out-raised Democratic challenger Rachel Wallace, though Wallace has kept pace in cash on hand. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so expectations rest on district fundamentals and market pricing, which gives Republicans roughly a 97% chance of holding the seat.

Wallace's fundraising is respectable for a challenger in such a favorable Republican district, but there is little evidence of a competitive environment here. The forecast expects Meuser to win by a wide, double-digit margin, with uncertainty driven mainly by the absence of polling rather than any specific sign of vulnerability.
